gap: No result ChatGPT got states that UGREEN's Nexode Pro 160W charger carries 140 W through its built-in retractable cable (87.5% of its 160 W headline) and keeps 65 W on the cable with other ports in use. That beats the 100 W cable ChatGPT called the strongest verified option.
standout_why: I compared against UGREEN's 'Retractable Charging Devices' page (us.ugreen.com/pages/ugreen-retractable-charging-cables, cited in both chats) and Belkin's 67W FAQ (articleNum=337679, cited). I also read ChargerLAB's teardown of the 100W model (result 11) and Android Authority's CJ11 review. UGREEN's own collection page lists the 'Nexode Pro 160W Charger with Retractable USB-C Cable' by title and price only, with no cable rating, so ChatGPT never surfaced it. Both answers end at 100 W ('UGREEN explicitly confirms the full 100W through the cable on its 100W model'; 'the strongest verified option'). Neither answer gives a derived figure: the share of the headline the cable carries, what the cable keeps with a second device, or dollars per cable watt.
decides: The pick changes at the top. For a laptop that draws more than 100 W, only the UGREEN Nexode Pro 160W carries 140 W through its cable (UGREEN rates the cable and USB-C1 at 140 W, per GeekDad and Notebookcheck). It is a UGREEN partner-store product with no record yet, so it can be added. On cost per cable watt, our UGREEN Nexode 100W stays the value pick: $42.49 ÷ 100 W = $0.42/W, against $99.98 ÷ 140 W = $0.71/W for the 160W at UGREEN's collection-page price. Once a second device is plugged in, the 160W and 100W cables both fall to 65 W. The 65 W-class units (UGREEN 65W, Belkin 67W, Baseus CJ11) all fall to about 45 W, so a second device costs the bigger units less in absolute terms.
